title: No Laughing in the Study Room: 45-Second Comedy Skit Script for 3
description: A 45-second vertical comedy script for 3 friends: first to laugh in a silent study room buys lunch, as a chair and a stomach team up. Free to film.
h1: No Laughing in the Study Room: a 45-Second Comedy Script for 3 Friends
logline: Three friends in a silent study room make a bet: the first to laugh buys lunch. Then a chair starts to squeak, a stomach starts to answer it, and holding a straight face turns into a battle.
setting: A quiet study room, classroom or kitchen table dressed as one. Props: books, a pen, a sticky note, one squeaky chair or a squeak added in the edit.

roles.name: Min
roles.note: Teen to 20s, any gender, makes the bet, very competitive.

roles.name: Alex
roles.note: Teen to 20s, any gender, sits in the squeaky chair, tries far too hard to fix it.

roles.name: Leo
roles.note: Teen to 20s, any gender, the calm one who is sure they will win.

script.text: ON SCREEN: Silent study room. First to laugh buys lunch.

script.action: MIN, ALEX and LEO sit at one table, books open, faces dead serious.
Alex shifts. The chair lets out a long, slow squeak.
Leo bites a pen. Min stares at the ceiling.
Alex tries to sit still. Slower. The squeak goes higher, like a question.
Min's stomach growls. Two notes. Exactly like the chair.

script.say: Did your stomach just answer my chair?

script.action: Leo slides over a sticky note: a drawing of the chair and the stomach holding hands.
Min shakes silently, tears running. Not one sound.
Leo, calm, turns a page. The page squeaks.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 with the phone on a stack of books at the end of the table so all three faces fit in the wide shot. Real laughing will ruin takes, so shoot each close-up separately and expect many tries; the outtakes make a good second video. Record the squeaks and the stomach growl separately, or make them with your mouth into the phone, and add them in the edit at the same volume each time. Use a real room with permission and no strangers in it, or dress a kitchen table as a study room.

ul: Everyone plays it as a life-or-death exam. The more serious the faces, the funnier each sound becomes.
Whisper every line. If any line is spoken at normal volume the room stops feeling silent.
Alex's fix should make things worse: slower movement means a longer squeak, so lean into the slow motion.
Min's silent laugh is the peak. Shoulders, tears, hand over mouth, but no sound at all until the snort lands.
Leo must stay perfectly calm until the page. The surprise is that the calm one breaks on the smallest sound.
Common mistake: adding a real prank on people nearby. Keep every gag inside the friend group.
Move it to a quiet waiting room or a train carriage with only your group in it, and change the bet to who carries the bags.
Play it with two friends, merging Leo and Min, or with four, adding someone who hums when nervous.
Different ending: nobody laughs, they all win, then the timer on the phone beeps and all three break at once.

faq.q: Can we film this in a real library?
faq.a: Only with permission and when nobody else is studying there. Do not film or disturb strangers. A classroom after hours or a kitchen table with a few books looks just as good on a phone.

faq.q: How do we stop laughing for real during takes?
faq.a: You will not, at first. Shoot the close-ups one person at a time, have the others look away, and roll for several takes. Keep the outtakes; they are a ready-made second video.

faq.q: Can we use it for a monetised channel or a class project?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0 for both. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the caption or the end card.
